facts.text: Lindy was named after aviator Charles Lindbergh—nicknamed “Lucky Lindy”—after his 1927 nonstop flight from New York to Paris.
The town was founded in 1928 as a small rural community in western Knox County, emerging late in Nebraska's settlement history.
Lindy sits 7 miles south of the Missouri River and the South Dakota border, in the valley of Hobo Creek.
Before European contact, the Ponca, Omaha, and Santee Sioux tribes used the river valleys around present‑day Lindy for hunting, farming, and seasonal villages.
Early settlers opened a general store and hoped a railroad would reach Lindy, but the line never materialized, a common rural challenge.
Lindy lies near the confluence of the Niobrara and Missouri Rivers, where low‑lying areas have flooded historically, including the 1881 Niobrara flood.
